correctness.rationale: For every n >= 5 the DIM/white-independent/black-one-regular equivalence yields exact local equations. Summing forces five to divide n. Eliminating the inner indicator gives Phi_3(T)Phi_5(T)z=0; Bezout splits the outer indicator into 3- and 5-periodic parts. Coprime CRT residues and the proved binary additive rectangle lemma force a single period; white density 2/5 excludes period three. Independent white vertices leave exactly five 5-periodic rotations and uniquely force the inner white pattern; these produce the five disjoint explicit matchings. Closed edge neighborhoods in cubic graphs show that every color class of a strong five-edge coloring is a DIM, forcing a unique partition up to names. Independently executed complete exact-cover enumeration for n=5..40 and the 346-state/576-arc finite-state all-length certificate reproduce the theorem. Proof includes the wraparound n=5 and all quantifiers; finite tests are supplementary.

originality.rationale: Exact enumeration and uniqueness are not consequences of previously published existence criteria. Full 2016 primary text (Section 3.5 Theorem 3.9) states that the specific perfect bicoloring quotient matrix occurs iff 5 divides n and gives ONE pattern, not the full count or uniqueness. Full 2021 arXiv primary text characterizes cubic five-edge-colorability as Petersen covering and provides nonunique coverings elsewhere, without classifying GP(n,2) covers. The 2021 uniqueness of the base graph, 2018 same-object index article, and 2024 DIM construction are credited; neither available statement establishes five DIMs and 120 color-named colorings. Focused semantic/database and published literature search found no dominating implication. Missing full index text/unindexed results remain disclosed risks.
residual_risks: Full text of Yang and Wu (2018) not accessed; an apparently stronger complete-coloring classification there or in supplementary material cannot be excluded.
Only the indexed Observation 7 passage of Mahmoodi et al. (2024) could be examined; covering statements elsewhere in that paper are possible.
Some older 1990 existence literature and unindexed research sources are inaccessible; a statement equivalent to five DIMs cannot be conclusively ruled out by partitioned searches.
No independent mathematical referee or external scientific audit has confirmed publication novelty.

value.rationale: Knowing there exists an efficient edge-dominating set, the parameter quotient matrix, or even the strong chromatic index does not determine all colorings. The theorem gives a complete infinite-family classification, an exact labelled count, and an all-orders unique optimal edge partition. A spectral-factor plus 3x5 binary-rectangle argument explains global rigidity; a finite transfer digraph gives an independent exact-state certificate. The contrast with known nonrigid cubic Petersen covers motivates why rigidity of this specific cyclic subfamily is mathematically significant. This is not merely a graph-specific small-count computation, a restatement of existing existence, or an unmotivated parameter slice.
